rv.q: It’s a rare musical that can warm your heart and chill you to the bone all at once – and that makes 'The Witches' essential viewing for all but the most sensitive kids. It’s a festive nightmare, electrifying as a failed bid to untangle your broken fairy lights, and just as sparkling.

" I’ll admit that, perhaps because of the Olivier’s treacherous acoustics, I wasn’t able to catch every syllable of the quicksilver lyrics. If I’m being ultra-critical, I’d add that the mechanised mice were a tad slow. But don’t be put off: this is a stunning achievement.

‘The Witches’ really is for everyone, (everyone over eight anyway). Because it’s quite easily the funniest new musical London has seen since at least ‘The Book of Mormon’. ... NT has thrown absolutely everything it has at ‘The Witches’, and the results are pure magic.

The scariness of childhood and the fear of death are present and correct, as is an awareness of economic or social difference…There are occasional lacunae here but this is a polished, witty, crisply sardonic serving of Dahl. And if the other child actors sharing the central roles are as good as the ones I saw, they deserve all the plaudits.

For all its naughty fun, the show is still brave enough to stick with Dahl’s very compromised sort-of happy ending...It may need a final pinch or two of magic, but this wickedly entertaining show will surely put a mischievous grin on anyone’s face.
There is fun, wit and imagination in Lyndsey Turner’s production...Lucy Kirkwood brings the magic through a script stuffed with effervescent one-liners.
"Some have accused The Witches of being misogynistic. It’s not so much that its slant feels hugely problematic here, more that it’s not massively dramatic.

The show is aimed at those aged eight and over; there is nothing that will give anyone nightmares here...The length, at nearly three hours including interval, may be a bit of a stretch for younger audience members and a few sections of the second half meander a little. However, most of the production whips by in a stream of pure entertainment.

Fans of this Roald Dahl story will be overjoyed at seeing The Witches brought to life on stage, although more Halloween than Christmas, this feels like a perfect festive alternative to pantomime or Dickins

There’s something resolutely original and unashamedly fun about this latest Dahl musical makeover. My nine year-old loved it, and proudly told me on the way out that she hadn’t been scared. Whether that’s quite the intention, I’m not sure, but I for one am glad it won’t induce nightmares in another generation.

Having roared through the plot in the first half it feels like the play has screeched to a halt...due to the sudden decline in quality this will only be of interest to those who truly love Roald Dahl and musicals, but even then I’d only recommend the cheapest of seats.

With truly impressive production values, a strikingly brilliant cast, and a book that retains the essence of the story while boldly bringing something new to it, ‘The Witches’ is a resounding success.
